name: Talivia
tagline: Open-source, self-hosted revenue-first analytics for founders
description: Talivia is a self-hosted analytics platform that puts revenue at the center instead of vanity metrics. Its open-source edition combines web analytics, session replay, revenue attribution, and customer revenue integrations into a single dashboard. You install a tracking snippet on your site, then connect payment providers such as Stripe, LemonSqueezy, Polar, Dodo, and Yolfi to tie visits directly to subscription lifecycle, refunds, disputes, and first- or last-touch attribution. It runs on PostgreSQL with a Prisma-backed Next.js app, ships as a single Docker Compose stack, and requires just two settings — a database URL and an app secret. A companion open-source Agent Kit adds an MCP server so AI coding agents can install tracking, verify events, and connect visits to payments.
highlights: Revenue-first analytics: web analytics, session replay, and payment attribution in one stack
Integrates Stripe, LemonSqueezy, Polar, Dodo, and Yolfi with full subscription lifecycle tracking
Self-hosted with a single Docker Compose stack and PostgreSQL
First- and last-touch attribution tied to real payment events
Optional open-source Agent Kit with an MCP server for AI coding agents
curatorNote: Launched in-window and already past 1.2k stars, Talivia is unusual because it frames analytics around revenue rather than page views. As a self-hostable alternative to hosted product-analytics tools, it is a strong candidate for founders who want their data and their attribution on their own hardware.
